reason: Reading PROV-XML with a bundleContent that has no id, a bundleContent nested in a bundle, or an unknown prov:frob element raises ProvXMLException with the exact message and no cause. The exception tree in docs/reference/serializers.md makes ProvXMLException the PROV-XML reader's error, and the ProvSerializationError docstring rendered there says that a fault the reader finds itself has no cause (#653).

A model rejection met while reading a bundle or an element raises the format's reader error, whose message starts with the record's label and continues with the model's message, and whose cause is the model's exception. The ProvSerializationError docstring, which docs/reference/serializers.md renders, says that a reader's error locates the record or the declaration, carries the model's sentence and sets the model's exception as the cause (#653).

Reading Turtle with a subject IRI urn:example:e2= typed prov:Entity raises ProvRDFException with the message `Cannot split IRI 'urn:example:e2=' into a namespace and a local part: it contains no '#' or '/' separator.` and no cause. The exception tree in docs/reference/serializers.md makes ProvRDFException the PROV-O reader's error, and the ProvSerializationError docstring rendered there says that a fault the reader finds itself has no cause (#653).

An etree element built in code, so with no source line, that is an unknown `prov:frob` raises `ProvXMLException` from `ProvXMLSerializer.deserialize_subtree` whose message starts at the element and its id, `<prov:frob> 'ex:a1'`, with no line prefix. The `ProvSerializationError` docstring rendered in docs/reference/serializers.md says a reader's error locates the record (#653). The test is the only guard of the branch of `_line` that adds nothing when `sourceline` is None, which `_element_position` relies on. The judge planted `return f"line {element.sourceline}, "` in `_line` and ran the whole suite, and only this test failed (1 failed, 5302 passed). No public call reaches that branch. Every element `ProvXMLSerializer.deserialize` parses has a line, and `ProvXMLSerializer.deserialize_subtree` is not rendered under docs/reference/ or frozen by test_public_api.py. The maintainer chose to leave the test and the branch as they are until a caller who passes an etree built in code turns up or the method is made public.

The reader errors of the JSON, XML, PROV-O and PROV-JSONLD formats, and ProvFormatNotDetected, are not subclasses of ProvException. The exception tree in docs/reference/serializers.md puts ProvSerializationError beside ProvException, and only ProvNSyntaxError carries both bases (#653).

The reader error of each of the five formats, and ProvFormatNotDetected, is a subclass of ProvSerializationError. The exception tree in docs/reference/serializers.md makes every reader error and ProvFormatNotDetected derive from ProvSerializationError, and docs/howto/read-write.md lists `except ProvSerializationError` as the catch for a failure to read or write in any format (#653).

Calling serialize on a serializer built with document None raises the format's own error class with the message `No document to serialize.` and writes nothing to the stream, with ProvSerializationError for PROV-N and PROV-JSON. docs/howto/read-write.md lists the writers' error for a serializer with no document under `except ProvSerializationError`, and the exception tree in docs/reference/serializers.md gives each format its error class (#653).

ProvNSyntaxError is also a ProvException, ProvSerializationError derives from prov.Error, ProvFormatNotDetected is a TypeError, ProvValueError is a ValueError, and DoNotExist is neither a ProvSerializationError nor a ProvException. The exception tree in docs/reference/serializers.md marks ProvNSyntaxError as also a ProvException, ProvValueError as also a ValueError, ProvFormatNotDetected as also a TypeError, and DoNotExist as a direct child of prov.Error (#653).
